turns.user: Acme Logistics bought 30% of Nordic Farms. Nordic Farms owns 60% of Greenfield Bank. What share of Greenfield Bank does Acme control indirectly? Explain step by step.
turns.raw:
Assuming “Acme” means ⟦COMPANY_1⟧:

1. ⟦COMPANY_1⟧ owns 30% of ⟦COMPANY_2⟧.
2. ⟦COMPANY_2⟧ owns 60% of ⟦COMPANY_3⟧.
3. Indirect economic ownership in ⟦COMPANY_3⟧ = 30% × 60% = 18%.

So Acme/⟦COMPANY_1⟧ has an 18% indirect economic interest in ⟦COMPANY_3⟧.

Important distinction: “control” is not the same as multiplying percentages. Acme controls ⟦COMPANY_3⟧ only if its 30% stake in ⟦COMPANY_2⟧ actually gives it control of ⟦COMPANY_2⟧—e.g. board control, voting agreement, veto/de facto control—and ⟦COMPANY_2⟧’s 60% gives control of ⟦COMPANY_3⟧. If 30% does not confer control of ⟦COMPANY_2⟧, Acme likely controls 0% of ⟦COMPANY_3⟧, though it is exposed to 18% economically. If 30% does confer control of ⟦COMPANY_2⟧, then Acme indirectly controls ⟦COMPANY_3⟧ through the chain, while its indirect ownership economics remain 18%.
